chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from 'Amr ibn Jubayr al-'Arzami, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

One who recites Surah Saad on the night of Friday will be given from the goodness of this world and the hereafter such that no one among people is given except a messenger prophet or a near angel. Allah will admit him to Paradise and everyone he loves from his family, even his servant whom he serves, even if they are not among those whose intercession can be done by him.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Saad on the night of Friday?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, the night of Friday (Laylat al-Jumu'ah) is considered a time of heightened spiritual potency, making this specific recitation particularly meritorious. The promise of including servants in Paradise, even if not part of the immediate family, underscores the concept of 'shafa'ah' (intercession) and the expansive mercy of the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the socio-spiritual dynamics of early Islamic households.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from ’Amru b. Jubayr al-’Arzami from his father from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said: “

One who recites Surah Saad every Friday eve would get goodness in this world and hereafter so much, which is not received by anyone except the prophets, messengers and nearest angels. Allah would make him and his family enter Paradise even if they are not among the ones whose intercession can be done by him.”
